title: Preprint Servers’ Policies, Submission Requirements, and Transparency in Reporting and Research Integrity Recommendations
extended_summary:
This paper does not match the requested direct secondary study, "Impact of ChatGPT on the Academic Writing Quality of Senior High School Students" (2024). Instead, it is a cross-sectional study examining the policies, submission requirements, and transparency/research-integrity recommendations of 57 preprint servers. The authors investigate how preprint servers present guidance to authors, what moderation and screening practices they describe, and the extent to which they encourage transparent reporting and research integrity standards.

The study’s approach was a structured review of publicly available webpages and submission platforms for 57 preprint servers accessed between January and March 2020. The authors extracted information on seven policy areas, six submission requirement areas, and eighteen transparency and research-integrity topics. This was not an educational intervention study and did not involve students, teachers, or schools. Instead, the units of analysis were preprint server websites and their stated policies.

The context is scholarly communication infrastructure rather than an educational setting. The authors found that most servers specified scope and moderation procedures, but very few addressed transparency and research integrity in depth. Across 18 possible transparency topics, servers addressed a median of only 1 topic, with data sharing, plagiarism, and ORCID use being the most commonly mentioned.

The main conclusion is that preprint servers generally provide limited guidance on transparent reporting and research integrity, despite their growing role in research dissemination. The authors argue that servers could do substantially more to promote better reporting practices, clearer screening standards, and stronger support for research integrity.
quality_tier_rationale: The provided document is not the requested education study; it is a 2021 preprint/research article about preprint server policies and contains no educational intervention, student sample, or writing-outcome methodology. As evidence for the target retrieval, it is a mismatched, non-relevant source and cannot support causal or descriptive inference about ChatGPT and student writing.
impact_tier_rationale: This paper reports no student learning or writing outcomes related to ChatGPT or any educational technology intervention, so there is no extractable impact for the requested topic.
